QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_9

question.text: Manoj purchased 1,000 units of a mutual fund scheme (60% in listed domestic equities, 40% in debt — so the fund holds less than 65% in debt/money-market instruments and is therefore NOT a Specified Mutual Fund Type 1 under Section 50AA) on 10th May 2023 at NAV of Rs.100. He sold all units on 20th May 2026 at NAV of Rs.140. How is the capital gain of Rs.40,000 taxed?

answer.text: Always short-term capital gain at slab rate under Section 50AA since it is a specified mutual fund
Short-term capital gain at 20% under Section 111A since it is an equity-oriented fund
Long-term capital gain at 12.5% since the units were bought after 1-4-2023, sold on/after 1-4-2025, and the fund is a listed scheme held for more than 12 months
Long-term capital gain at 12.5% with indexation benefit since holding exceeds 36 months

explanation.text: The Logic: Because the fund holds only 40% in debt (less than the 65% threshold), it does NOT meet the "Specified Mutual Fund Type 1" definition under Section 50AA. It is also not an equity-oriented fund for tax purposes (which requires the higher equity-oriented threshold). Under the post-1-4-2023 transitional rule for "other mutual funds" / Specified MF Type 2, units bought after 1-4-2023 and sold on/after 1-4-2025 attract normal capital gains rules: a holding period of more than 12 months for a listed scheme qualifies for LTCG at 12.5% without indexation. Manoj held from May 2023 to May 2026 (~36 months > 12 months), so LTCG at 12.5% applies. The Trap: Option A would apply only to a Specified Mutual Fund Type 1 (>=65% debt) under Section 50AA — but this fund has only 40% debt, so Section 50AA does not apply. Option B treats it as equity-oriented STCG, which is incorrect for the holding period and the fund's classification. Option D wrongly assumes indexation benefit, which is not available under the new 12.5% LTCG rule. Note: NISM Series X-B workbook (pages 177-178, 215-216) defines Specified MF Type 1 as funds with >=65% in debt/money-market instruments (always short-term under Section 50AA). The fund here at 40% debt is outside that bucket and is therefore subject to ordinary capital gains rules under the transitional regime.
